notes: Checked and failed on refresh rate alone: 60 Hz maximum, with a 56-76 Hz vertical scan range, confirmed by several retailer tables and contradicted by none. Everything else about it is what you asked for - IPS Black at 2000:1, 90 W USB-C, KVM, height-adjustable - which is exactly why it belongs in the rejected list rather than being left out. It is the previous generation of the U3425WE and sits one digit away in the model code, so without this entry as a negative match a shop listing for the cheaper 60 Hz model could be read as the 120 Hz one. The builder rejects it from the 100 Hz floor on its own; no reject_reason is set by hand.

Checked and failed on refresh rate: Asus's own spec page gives 60 Hz maximum (48-60 Hz range) and a 3800R curve, which is nearly flat. Recorded because it is easy to confuse with two other ProArt 34s - the PA348CGV on the watchlist, which is 120 Hz, and the PA34VC, which Asus lists at 100 Hz with a 1900R curve. The 96 W power delivery here is Asus's figure, not the 90 W often repeated. The PA34VC is not on either list: it looks like it would qualify at 100 Hz, but its stand and resolution were not verified in this round, so it is left for Discover to surface rather than entered on a guess.

Checked at this exact model and rejected on panel family, not on specs. Worth knowing what is being turned down: 120 Hz over DisplayPort and USB-C, 100 W power delivery, KVM, Gigabit Ethernet, a 1440p Windows Hello webcam and a 3000:1 native contrast - on paper one of the best pure work monitors at this size. It fails only because VA was excluded from the wanted families. If you ever want it back, tick VA on the Settings page and rebuild; the entry is complete enough to qualify immediately. The rejection is no longer written by hand: the criteria gate panel family directly, so this entry states its panel and the reason follows from whatever families are wanted at the time.

Checked across retailer tables and rejected on panel family. 100 Hz, 90 W USB-C, KVM and Ethernet on a 1000R curved VA panel at 3000:1. The suffix decides the ports on this line - UAN, TAU, TAN and VAN variants differ over Thunderbolt 4 and a webcam, and the webcam VC version is listed as discontinued - so the aliases cover the forms seen rather than a bare 'S34C650'. HDR10 is mentioned in listings but no DisplayHDR tier, so the field is left empty.
